::: {#fig-newton-model}

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}

### R

```{r}
#| label: newton-model-r
#| fig-alt: >-
#|   Plot of the cubic f of x equals x cubed over 3 minus 4 x for x from 0.5
#|   to 4, in blue, and its quadratic model at x equal to 2.5 in dashed
#|   vermilion. The model touches the cubic at 2.5, is a parabola opening
#|   upward, and has its lowest point at 2.05, marked by a vermilion triangle.
#|   A vermilion circle marks the starting point 2.5, and a blue square marks
#|   the minimizer 2 of the cubic.
#| fig-height: 4
#| fig-width: 6
nm_x_fn <- seq(0.5, 4, length.out = 301)
nm_f_fn <- function(x) x^3 / 3 - 4 * x
nm_q_fn <- function(x) {
  nm_f_fn(2.5) + 2.25 * (x - 2.5) + 2.5 * (x - 2.5)^2
}
nm_curve_fn <- tibble::tibble(x = nm_x_fn, y = nm_f_fn(nm_x_fn))
nm_model_fn <- tibble::tibble(x = nm_x_fn, y = nm_q_fn(nm_x_fn))
nm_start_fn <- tibble::tibble(x = 2.5, y = nm_f_fn(2.5))
nm_step_fn <- tibble::tibble(x = 2.05, y = nm_q_fn(2.05))
nm_min_fn <- tibble::tibble(x = 2, y = nm_f_fn(2))
nm_aes_fn <- ggplot2::aes(x, y)
ggplot2::ggplot(nm_curve_fn, nm_aes_fn) +
  ggplot2::geom_line(colour = "#0072B2") +
  ggplot2::geom_line(
    data = nm_model_fn, colour = "#D55E00", linetype = "dashed"
  ) +
  ggplot2::geom_point(data = nm_start_fn, colour = "#D55E00", size = 3) +
  ggplot2::geom_point(
    data = nm_step_fn, colour = "#D55E00", size = 3, shape = 17
  ) +
  ggplot2::geom_point(
    data = nm_min_fn, colour = "#0072B2", size = 3, shape = 15
  ) +
  ggplot2::coord_cartesian(ylim = c(-8, 0)) +
  ggplot2::labs(x = "x", y = "value")
```

### Python

```{python}
#| label: newton-model-python
#| fig-alt: >-
#|   Plot of the cubic f of x equals x cubed over 3 minus 4 x for x from 0.5
#|   to 4, in blue, and its quadratic model at x equal to 2.5 in dashed
#|   vermilion. The model touches the cubic at 2.5, is a parabola opening
#|   upward, and has its lowest point at 2.05, marked by a vermilion triangle.
#|   A vermilion circle marks the starting point 2.5, and a blue square marks
#|   the minimizer 2 of the cubic.
#| fig-height: 4
#| fig-width: 6
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

nm_x_fn = np.linspace(0.5, 4, 301)
nm_f_fn = lambda x: x**3 / 3 - 4 * x
nm_q_fn = lambda x: nm_f_fn(2.5) + 2.25 * (x - 2.5) + 2.5 * (x - 2.5) ** 2
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 4), layout="constrained")
ax.plot(nm_x_fn, nm_f_fn(nm_x_fn), color="#0072B2", label="f")
ax.plot(nm_x_fn, nm_q_fn(nm_x_fn), "--", color="#D55E00",
        label="quadratic model at 2.5")
ax.plot(2.5, nm_f_fn(2.5), "o", color="#D55E00", markersize=8)
ax.plot(2.05, nm_q_fn(2.05), "^", color="#D55E00", markersize=8)
ax.plot(2, nm_f_fn(2), "s", color="#0072B2", markersize=8)
ax.set_ylim(-8, 0)
ax.set_xlabel("x")
ax.set_ylabel("value")
ax.legend(loc="upper center")
plt.show();
```

:::

The [cubic](algebra.qmd#def-cubic-polynomial) $f(x) = \tfrac{1}{3} x^3 - 4x$ and its [quadratic model](#def-quadratic-model) at $x = 2.5$.
The model touches $f$ at $2.5$ (circle),
and its [minimizer](algebra.qmd#def-global-minimizer) $2.05$ (triangle) is the iterate after one [Newton step](#def-newton-step) from $2.5$ (@exm-newton-model).
It lies close to the minimizer $2$ of $f$ (blue marker).

:::
